abstract: The NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is developing a standardized, integrated reference framework for classifying and studying brain cell types across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse. We present a cross-species, multimodal atlas of the basal ganglia, a group of subcortical nuclei central to motor control, adaptive behavior, and neurological disease. Built from large-scale single-cell transcriptomic classification and integrated with epigenomic, spatial genomic, multiomic, and developmental datasets, the atlas provides a curated, data-driven taxonomy with standardized nomenclature, extensive phenotypic characterization, and community-informed annotation. Cell types are mapped into species-specific anatomical reference frameworks and linked across species through structural ontologies. Realizing this resource required coordinated standards for tissue acquisition and processing, harmonized donor metadata, anatomical registration, sequencing pipelines, data infrastructure, visualization, mapping tools, and interoperable metadata. The BICAN basal ganglia atlas demonstrates how pipelines and standards can be implemented, validated, and scaled toward a whole-brain human and mammalian cell-type reference.
